anomalies.observed: The LM2576 buck converter's Schottky diode D41 has its cathode on the switch-node/inductor net (Net-(D41-K)) and its anode tied to the +5V output rail instead of GND.
anomalies.expected: A standard LM2576 buck converter requires a freewheel/catch diode with cathode at U13 pin 2 / L2 pin 1 and anode at GND. Connecting the diode anode to +5V leaves no correct freewheel path and places the diode across the output/switch node in the wrong reference direction.
anomalies.impact: The 5V rail is unlikely to regulate correctly; the inductor current has no proper freewheel path, and D41 can discharge the +5V output into the switch node, potentially preventing boot or damaging the regulator.

anomalies.observed: U16 is configured for SPI (pin 9 tied low) but its A0/~CS pin 10 is tied directly to GND, while U25's A0/~CS pin 10 is driven by Module2 GPIO18. Both U16 and U25 SO pins are connected to the same MISO net NET0206.
anomalies.expected: In a shared SPI bus, each slave's ~CS must be controlled so that only one slave drives MISO at a time. Tying U16 ~CS permanently low selects it continuously and creates contention with U25 on the shared SPI bus.
anomalies.impact: U16 will drive the SPI MISO line whenever powered, preventing reliable access to U25 and corrupting SPI reads when both slaves are selected.
